cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the church in Corinth, where false apostles have been boasting (2 Corinthians 1:1; 11:13-18). Since many are boasting, Paul boasts too, and he admits he's speaking as a fool (2 Corinthians 11:18, 21). Now he's in a FULL brag, friend, and he says he must go on boasting, even though there's nothing to gain.

cards.question: Paul says there's nothing to gain, but he keeps boasting anyway. What does he move on to?

answers.text: Visions and revelations from the Lord
Praise he got from the other churches
His years of training as a Pharisee

cards.text: Paul says he knows a man in Christ who was caught up to the third heaven FOURTEEN years ago. Friend, I can't remember what I stamped this morning.

cards.question: Paul says he knows for sure whether the man was in his body when he was caught up to the third heaven.

cards.text: Paul circles back to it: in the body or out of it, he doesn't know, but God knows. And this man was caught up to Paradise.

cards.question: The man was caught up to Paradise. What does Paul say about the things he heard there?

answers.text: No one is permitted to tell them
Every church needs to hear them
He wrote them all down later

cards.question: Paul will boast about a man like that. But when it comes to himself, he'll boast only in his weaknesses.

cards.text: Then Paul talks about what it would be like if he did boast about himself. Even if he wanted to, he says he'd be speaking the truth.

cards.question: Paul says that if he wanted to boast about himself, he would be a fool.

cards.text: But Paul holds back anyway. He doesn't want anyone giving him more credit than what they see in him or hear from him, or because of these surpassingly great revelations.

cards.question: After those surpassingly great revelations, Paul says he was given something. What was it?
Paul says the thorn in his flesh was given to keep him from becoming ___.
Paul calls the thorn in his flesh a messenger of Satan, sent to torment him.

cards.text: So Paul takes that thorn to the Lord and pleads with Him to take it away. Friend, I get ONE crumb stuck in my mustache and start acting like I need a doctor.

cards.question: Paul pleads with the Lord to take the thorn away from him. How many times?
Paul has pleaded three times for the thorn to go. What does the Lord say to him?

answers.text: My grace is sufficient for you
My hand will lift it from you

cards.question: The Lord tells Paul why His grace is sufficient: His power is perfected in ___.
Now Paul says he'll boast all the more gladly in his weaknesses. Why?

answers.text: So the power of Christ may rest on him
So the Corinthians will pray for him
So the false apostles will stop bragging

cards.text: That's why, for the sake of Christ, Paul DELIGHTS in weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions and difficulties. Friend, I can't even delight in a burnt batch.

cards.question: Paul sums it all up: when he is weak, then he is ___.

findings.problem: The stop relies on discovery questions well beyond a few. Cards 2, 4, 6, 7, 11, 13, 15 and 16 ask for details or wording that cannot be reasoned out from the earlier cards, leaving the baker to guess.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The question is not self-contained. "A man like that" points back to earlier cards without identifying the man as the one who was caught up to the third heaven and Paradise.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
